Methods Text

Ready-to-paste text for the Methods section of your manuscript

Full paragraph
Quality control was performed using AnnQC v0.1.0 (Weisberg, 2026). Mitochondrial genes were identified by the 'MT-' prefix and ribosomal genes by the 'RPS|RPL' prefix. Cells were filtered using MAD-based adaptive thresholds derived from the data distribution: mitochondrial content ≤ 17.3%, gene count between 601 and 4171 genes per cell, minimum UMI count of 1440. Gene-level filtering removed genes expressed in fewer than 3 cells. Doublet detection was not performed or was skipped. After quality control, following established best practices, 10,203 of 11,769 cells were retained (86.7%). Sensitivity analysis was performed using annqc sensitivity to assess the impact of threshold choices on cell retention and cluster composition, using independent threshold sweeps and combined strict/standard/permissive MAD-based profiles. AnnQC does not perform ambient RNA correction; tools such as CellBender or SoupX should be applied upstream if ambient RNA removal is required. All QC parameters and software versions are recorded in adata.uns['annqc'] for full reproducibility.
Short version (for abstracts)
scRNA-seq data were quality controlled using AnnQC v0.1.0 with MAD-based adaptive thresholds, retaining 10,203 of 11,769 cells (86.7%) after removal of low-quality cells and doublets (ambient RNA correction not performed). Threshold sensitivity was assessed with annqc sensitivity.

Scrublet citation: Wolock SL, Lopez R, Klein AM. Scrublet: Computational Identification of Cell Doublets in Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data. Cell Syst. 2019;8(4):281–291.

mito:
  prefix: MT-
  max_pct: 15
ribo:
  prefix: RPS|RPL
  max_pct: 50
cells:
  min_genes: 200
  max_genes: 4000
  min_counts: 500
  max_counts: null
genes:
  min_cells: 3
doublets:
  method: scrublet
  threshold: auto
  simulate_doublet_ratio: 2.0
normalization:
  method: log1p
  target_sum: 10000
thresholds:
  min_cells_pass: 100
  min_cells_warn: 500
  min_cells_pass_per_sample: 200
  min_cells_warn_per_sample: 500
